long_synopsis: Week 85 brought no single rupture, only repetition across nine fronts: voter-roll purges dressed as fraud enforcement, a Supreme Court petition to override a ballot-rule injunction, warrantless surveillance of journalists, fabricated war footage from Iran, a collapsing detention medical system, blocked accountability for an ICE shooting and an Epstein-linked witness, executive vanity projects, a split judiciary, and expanding license-plate surveillance. The Democracy Clock held at 7:40 p.m., its first flat week in a long stretch, but twenty-one traits moved beneath that stillness, all but one worsening. A whistleblower's disclosure and several court rulings offset an aggressive push into elections and detainees. Nothing broke. Nothing healed. The pressure simply continued, distributed across enough fronts that no single act looked extraordinary.
short_synopsis: A flat clock masked twenty-one moving traits as agencies turned voter rolls, ballots, journalists, and detainees into instruments of control. Courts, a whistleblower, and local officials held some lines. The week's stillness reflects offsetting forces, not calm.
